title: Minibeast Habitats
keyIdea: A micro-habitat is a tiny home, like the space under a log, the soil, a leaf or a pond. Each one has its own conditions: damp or dry, dark or light, wet or on land. Different minibeasts like different conditions, so you find different creatures in different places. Woodlice and worms like damp, dark places because they dry out in the sun. Butterflies and bees like sunny flowers. Pond snails live in water. When the weather changes, minibeasts move to stay where it suits them.
familyTip: Make a choice tray from a shoebox lid. Put damp kitchen roll on one half and dry paper on the other. Gently add five woodlice from under a log, cover with card, and peek after ten minutes. Count where they went, then put them back where you found them.

visual.caption: Which place suits it? Drag each minibeast to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: a slug on a hot day

lab.caption: Flagship lab: test woodlice in damp-or-dry and dark-or-light trays, match minibeasts to homes, and track them as the weather changes.

kid: A micro-habitat is a tiny home. Under a log is one. The soil is one. A pond is one too.
Each tiny home is different. Some are damp and dark. Some are sunny and dry. Some are full of water.
Woodlice and worms like damp, dark places. In the sun they dry out. Butterflies and bees like sunny flowers. Pond snails live in water.
Minibeasts move when the weather changes. On a hot day slugs hide under stones. When it rains, they come out to eat.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. In England, Year 2 science asks children to identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited, and to name a variety of animals in their habitats, including micro-habitats. Key words: habitat, micro-habitat, conditions, damp, dry, shade, suited, minibeast.

A common mistake is to think animals live somewhere by chance or because it is near people. Children also expect every animal in a test to go the same way; in a real choice chamber most woodlice gather on the damp side, but a few do not, so we look at what most of them do.

Woodlice are crustaceans that lose water through their body surface and breathe with gill-like parts that must stay moist, so they shelter in damp, dark places by day. Earthworms need moist skin to breathe. Slugs and snails come out in wet weather and at night, when drying out is less of a danger.

In the lab your child runs two choice tray tests (damp or dry, then dark or light), matches four minibeasts to homes, watches a woodlouse's water drop on a sunny path and carries it back, then finds slugs, bees and pond skaters as the weather changes.

practice.prompt: There are {a} woodlice in a tray. {b} go to the damp side. How many stay on the dry side?
practice.hint: Take the ones on the damp side away from all {a} woodlice.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. Most went to the damp side, because woodlice like damp places.

practice.prompt: Where is the best place to look for woodlice?
practice.hint: Woodlice dry out in the sun. They need somewhere damp and dark.
practice.explain: Under a log it stays damp and dark, so woodlice do not dry out.

practice.prompt: You lift a log and count {a} woodlice and {b} worms. How many minibeasts is that?
practice.hint: Add the woodlice and the worms together.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} minibeasts. A damp log is home to lots of them.

practice.prompt: A butterfly needs sun and nectar. Where will you see one?
practice.hint: Nectar comes from flowers. Butterflies warm up in the sun.
practice.explain: Butterflies visit flowers in sunny spots to sip nectar.

practice.prompt: It has just rained. Where will you find slugs?
practice.hint: Rain makes everything damp, so slugs are safe to come out.
practice.explain: When it is wet, slugs leave their hiding places to eat plants.

choices: a tiny home, like under a log
pool.hint: Micro means very small. Habitat means home.
pool.explain: A micro-habitat is a small home with its own conditions, like under a log or in a pond.

pool.prompt: Which minibeast lives in pond water?
pool.hint: Its name tells you its home.
pool.explain: A pond snail lives and feeds in the water. Woodlice and bees live on land.

pool.prompt: {a} woodlice go into a tray. {b} crawl under the dark bark. How many stay in the light?
pool.hint: Take the ones under the bark away from all of them.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. Most hide under the bark, because woodlice like dark places.

pool.prompt: Why do woodlice hide in damp, dark places?
choices: so they do not dry out
to keep warm in the sun
pool.hint: What happened to the woodlouse on the sunny path?
pool.explain: Sun and wind dry woodlice out. Damp, dark places keep their bodies moist.

pool.prompt: Mia says: 'One woodlouse went to the dry side, so woodlice like dry places.' What is wrong?
choices: most of them went to the damp side
pool.hint: Look at what most of the woodlice did, not just one.
pool.explain: Animals do not all do the same thing. 7 of 8 went to the damp side, so they like damp.

pool.prompt: Where would you look for an earthworm?
pool.hint: Worms need damp skin. They dig.
pool.explain: Earthworms tunnel through damp soil. On a hot path they would dry out.

pool.prompt: A hot, sunny afternoon. Where are the slugs?
pool.hint: Slugs dry out fast. Where is it cool and damp?
pool.explain: On a hot day slugs hide under stones and logs where it stays damp.

pool.prompt: You find {a} bees on the flowers and {b} under a stone. How many more bees are on the flowers?
pool.hint: Take the smaller number from the bigger one.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} more on the flowers. Bees need flowers for food.
